status: evaluation protocol prepared and smoke-tested on CPU; not yet frozen (inputs on the server are needed to fix hashes)
question: When the output sampling geometry is a general homography rather than a symmetric scale, does the analytic footprint response transfer without any warp training, and where does it matter: only where the footprint is anisotropic or rotated (LTEW/SRWarp in-scale and out-of-scale), or decisively where the output is coarser than the input (minification)?

protocols.ltew-warp: LTEW release: warped LR inputs with forward 3x3 matrices (.pth) and HR ground truth, in-scale and out-of-scale splits for Set5/Set14/B100/Urban100/DIV2K; output grid = HR; masked PSNR (Y, no shave) over pixels whose source lies inside the input, following LTEW's calc_mpsnr. Matrix convention (input px -> output px, integer centres) is checked on SRWarp's validation set, which ships ground truth: the bicubic-point baseline must reach a plausible PSNR; otherwise --invert-matrix.
protocols.ltew-asym: LTEW's 24 asymmetric pairs (three in-scale, three out-of-scale per dataset), LR by per-axis PIL bicubic exactly as LTEW's sr-asp-implicit-downsampled wrapper; evaluated as a diagonal homography through the same code path.
protocols.minify: our split: input = HR image, output = HR-sized grid under a perspective tilt with local minification (strength 0.3/0.6/0.9, fixed seed); reference = 8x8 supersampled bicubic backward warp, i.e. the box-filtered warp. Baselines: bicubic point warp (aliased) and the supersampled warp itself (upper bound).

footprints.token: LIIF, LTE, SC-INR with the axis-aligned cell = bounding box of the parallelogram J[-1/2,1/2]^2 (reduces to the exact per-axis cell for scaling)
footprints.jac: SC-INR and SC-INR-exact with the parallelogram footprint through the sinc response: W_k = sinc(w_k . J e_row) sinc(w_k . J e_col); for diagonal J identical to the cell path (verified to 0)

expectations_written_before_running.E1: ltew-warp in-scale: zero-shot models trained on symmetric scales lose to LTEW's published numbers (trained on warps); among them SC-INR >= LTE and the jac footprint >= token footprint by a small margin. This is a transfer check, not a claim of superiority.
expectations_written_before_running.E2: ltew-asym: reproduces the stage-01 ordering on LTEW's own pairs; out-of-scale pairs (one factor up to 8) widen the LTE gap.
expectations_written_before_running.E3: minify: bicubic-point aliases where local scale < 1; SC-INR (jac) and SC-INR-exact approach the supersampled reference, LIIF/LTE do not improve on bicubic-point there. This is the setting the footprint view is for; a failure here would falsify the practical value of the analytic response.
expectations_written_before_running.not_claimed: no PSNR superiority at symmetric in-range scales; LTEW-level warping quality without warp training

compute: inference only; LTEW sets about 400 images x 2 splits, minify 3 strengths per image; a few GPU-hours in total
